issues.title: CCA attester model
issues.author: thomas-fossati
issues.body:
The CCA attester model is slightly more complicated than is currently described.

There are _two_ separate sub-attesters (platform and realm) rather than one, each with their independent AE/TE split, and bound via RAK attestation.

This should be explained in Section 3 and illustrated in Figure 1.

issues.title: In delegated mode, should `eat_nonce` be `rak_pub_hash_value` instead?
issues.author: thomas-fossati
issues.body:
There is potential semantic ambiguity in using `eat_nonce` for the binder in delegated mode.

In particular,

1. it's not a proper challenge issued by the ABI caller
2. freshness properties associated with the claim are not clear.

It seems easier to create a new claim with explicit semantics, e.g., `rak_pub_hash_value`.

comments.author: SimonFrost-Arm
comments.body: Would better documentation for the usage of eat_nonce in this profile suffice? My concern about adding an explicit binder for delegate is ambiguity on presence or not of eat_nonce in the same platform report: should they both be there / what are there relation / if no eat_nonce then will profile implementers be confident of freshness?  Keeping eat_nonce allows re-use of the platform report in multiple layerings, including both binding and as a pure freshness challenge.

comments.author: gmandyam
comments.body:
I think the use of eat-nonce is consistent with https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9334#name-implicit-timekeeping-using-.  

This is because in this case the eat-nonce provides an implicit indication of time, namely the time at which the RAK was generated and bound to the platform token.

issues.title: algorithm ID claim string is discouraged?
issues.author: deeglaze
issues.body:
I'm reviewing the attestation design for our ARM silicon and I see

> The CCA platform hash algorithm ID claim is a text string that identifies the algorithm used to calculate the extended measurements in the CCA platform token.
> The string SHOULD be encoded according to "Hash Name String" in the "Named Information Hash Algorithm Registry" [IANA.named-information].

My understanding from Henk is that the text is discouraged and the number in [[IANA.named-information](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ffm-rats-cca-token-00.html#IANA.named-information)] is preferred. I'd like the text to allow for both with `text / int` and say

The CCA platform hash algorithm ID claim is a text string or integer that identifies the algorithm used to calculate the extended measurements int the CCA platform token.
> If the identifier is an integer, it MUST denote to the corresponding algorithm in the IANA.named-information hash algorithm registry.
> If the identifier is a string, it SHOULD be encoded according to "Hash Name String" in the "Named Information Hash Algorithm Registry" [IANA.named-information].


Similar for `cca-realm-hash-algo-id-label`, `cca-realm-public-key-hash-algo-id-label`.

comments.author: SimonFrost-Arm
comments.body: I'll review, but background is that pinning down a standard naming that corresponds to an IANA registry proved difficult. The named hash algo was a recommendation from IANA expert review. RFC6920, which established that registry, is text based and notes that the numeric ID is optional. Do you have a ref for the deprecation? We'll need a stable ref & usage for further IANA registration of evidence claims.

comments.author: thomas-fossati
comments.body:
> Do you have a ref for the deprecation?

I am not aware of any plans to deprecate the textual version in favor of its numeric counterpart.

The reason ID is optional is that the codepoint space is severely limited, with only 63 possible IDs, of which 12 are already allocated.

If the registry wants to have any chance of long-term survival, it **must** allow text.

I am unsure why this decision was made initially; it seems quite short-sighted, but we can't (easily) change that.

comments.author: deeglaze
comments.body: This was a comment from Henk, so perhaps it was a pet peeve and not the IETF zeitgeist.

comments.author: thomas-fossati

comments.body:
```suggestion
The Device TPM Binding Data claim holds data that can be used to prove that the TPM and the CCA HES belong to the same system.
```

```suggestion
The details of the binding data within this claim are Implementation Defined, as different underlying TPM binding schemes may be available.
```
Is the missing CDDL intentional or an oversight?

```suggestion
The type for this claim is `bstr`.
```
Since this type is exactly the same as the platform UEID (i.e., RAND), we can reuse `eat-ueid-rand-type` — which also happens to be more precisely defined.

```suggestion
REALM_FRAGS += cca-realm-devices-token-hash.cddl
```
Maybe we could provide more about its semantics.  E.g., what is it used for? What is the correlation between this claim and RIM (if any)?  And between this and REMs (again, if any)?
AFAICS, "cca-realm-devices-token" is not defined anywhere
